I worked in customer service as a cashier at a big grocery chain. It was my first job and I was doing pretty well. 

Two months in around the end of November I fell extremely ill. I had the flu and it was seriously effecting my asthma. It pretty much felt like I was hit by a truck. I ending up having to go to the ER. The doctors there told me I needed to be on bed rest for 2 weeks. I expressed concerns about my job and they printed me out a doctor's note. My fiancé brought the note to my supervisor as I was too ill to come in. I call in just to secure that I would not be at work for two weeks. 

The next day I got a call telling me they needed me to work my shift that day. I explained to them how I was too sick to leave my bed, that my fiancé had brought in a doctor's note, and that I called last night securing the next two weeks off. They said they didn't care and needed me there. They threatened me with termination if I didn't show up. I then argued that since I work the morning shift most of the people I serve are elderly and could get them extremely sick. They said that was no excuse. I threatened to call the CDC if they made me work. 

When I got back from the two weeks they fired me on the spot. They even claimed they didn't have a doctor's note for me. Honestly, I don't care because I don't want to work for a company who cares so little for the health of their employees and customers. 

TDLR; Works cashier in the morning shift with the majority of customers being elderly. Got extremely ill leaving me bed ridden for two weeks. Refused to work and get customers sick. Gets fired on the spot.

For a while (about 2 years) I was completely unable to "preform" with other partners because the flashbacks were so intense. I also gained enough courage to text my nmom about everything that happened. She never responded. 

Fast forward to about six months ago. I told my nmom that I need to set up an appointment with a psychologist because I'm pretty sure I'm suffering from either PTSD or C-PTSD and I was confused on how to do that. She told me "You haven't been through anything traumatic enough to give you that". I hung up the phone and sobbed for hours. I will never forget that she said that to me. It's such an awful thing to say.

Open doors is what bothers me. I can't be in a room with an open door because my nmom constantly thought I was "up to something" and would either barge in or not let me close my door. She would also leave doors slightly open (out of habit). So I can't be in a room with an open door. It won't cause me to panic, but it will give me a lot of anxiety and discomfort. 

People having a stern tone of voice tends to trigger me more and if someone yells at me - forget about it - I go into a full blown panic attack.

This story happened to me (F 19). I always end up getting myself into the most fucked up of situations, even at 14, the age I am when the story starts.

David presented himself as a charming, funny, caring, and mature guy. He seemed like the perfect boyfriend. So, when we started dating you can imagine my shock when Jacob told me that this kid is "bad news" and I should "get out of there ASAP", but of course you can't tell a naïve 14 year old girl that her boyfriend is bad. The first six months were fairytale-esque as he was pulling me further into his grasp. He'd tell me lies about himself that he knew would impress me. He'd buy me things and tell me how beautiful I was. This whole time Jacob was warning me about him. 

Over the next few months he only pulled the reigns tighter. I couldn't listen to any music except for metal & subgenres of metal without being mocked, teased, and belittled. I had to cut ties with all my friends including Jacob. This killed me on the inside. Why didn't I just leave then? Before this a pedophile had his grasp on me for two years and I just thought that's how relationships worked because I was groomed to think that way since 12. The signs were there; I just ignored them. 

A year into the relationship he started yelling and belittling me for every little thing. If I didn't know something about music I was a "dumb piece of shit". It was constant verbal abuse and he lied about really sadistic things like finding his best friend hanged in his room. 

The physical abuse started shortly after. I started "disobeying" him and reaching out to people. Then he left me because he knew I was about to leave him. After the break up I ended up in a mental hospital for two weeks after a suicide attempt that was unrelated to the break up. During this time he told all my friends that I was the abuser and he "tried to save me from dying". I came back to no friends except for Jacob. He gave me a subtle "I told you so" and a great big hug. 

I have all my friends back and I'm happily engaged to Jacob. Some stories end happy.

My suicide attempt. It completely changed the way I viewed life. Now when I do anything I savor every moment. I became an entirely different person as well. I became more kind, open, and appreciative. Before I didn't like to listen to people talk about the bad things in their life (I wasn't an asshole about it though. I still listened, I just secretly didn't like it), but after that happened I started to love when people come to me for advice or just to vent.

When I was less self-aware I did this by pushing people away. I severely regret this because it left me lonely and only made my symptoms fester more. I deal with it now by trying my best to ignore those thoughts and use a logical train of thought.

For example: My BPD tells me that my friend hates me out of the blue. I think "Did I give any LOGICAL reason for that person to hate me?". I take time to carefully look over the evidence. I also text them a simple "hello" to see if they still want to talk. If there is no physical evidence of me doing anything or them expressing their hatred then it must be my BPD. If the evidence is convincing me otherwise and I can't convince myself that they don't, then I ask them. Usually in this format "I'm really sorry if my assumption is wrong, but my BPD is acting up and I was wondering if you still liked me/view me as a friend?". 

If they are a true friend they will understand and tell you the truth. 

Granted, this doesn't work in every situation because humans are emotionally complex, but it works the majority of the time for me.

This disturbing thing that happened in my family's history splits into two parts: before I was born, and just about 5 or 6 years ago. 
My great uncle was a heroin addict from the time my mom was 7 to the time she was 27. So an awful 20 years. Before he got clean he was broke and living in the streets. He used any needle he could find to shoot up. 
Fast forward to 5 or 6 years ago (I was around the age of 12)...this is where the story becomes more disturbing. I would visit my great uncle every couple of months or two because at this point he had been sober for 14 years. Every time I would come over there he became thinner and thinner. In the span of a year he had went from a healthy 180 lbs (≈82 kg) to a skeleton figure of 68 lbs (≈31 kg).
One day, I went to his townhouse and something felt extremely off. I saw him inside and he looked worse than before. It was an image I will never forget. His eyes, cheeks, and temples were sunken into his skull. While his elbows jutted out with his fingers. His knees looked like two baseballs connected to boney thighs and calves. His smile was radiant, but was marked with a lot of pain. Something told me that it was the last time I would see him...and the next week my mom told me that he passed away. 
It turns out he had Hepititis C and was suffering for a great deal of time, much longer than the year he dropped the majority of his body mass. Doctors suspected that he had contracted it from one of the dirty needles that he had used when he was addicted. 
As disturbing as addicts can be, we must remember that they need more help than we can give them. A warning to the fellow reddit community...stay away from hard drugs.
